name: Denys-Drash Syndrome

criteria.description: Diffuse mesangial sclerosis causing early-onset nephrotic syndrome
Pathogenic mutation in the WT1 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including Wilms tumor, diffuse mesangial sclerosis, and gonadal dysgenesis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for WT1 mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met.

laboratory: Proteinuria and nephrotic range protein loss
Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
Abnormal hormone levels related to gonadal dysgenesis
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephromegaly or renal masses
Abdominal CT or MRI identifying Wilms tumor
other: Histopathology revealing diffuse mesangial sclerosis in renal biopsy
Gonadal biopsy showing streak gonads or dysgenetic gonadal tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly gonadal dysgenesis without Wilms tumor
WAGR syndrome features absent in Denys-Drash

redFlags: Rapidly progressive nephrotic syndrome in infancy
Development of Wilms tumor in early childhood
Ambiguous genitalia or gonadal dysgenesis in a child with renal disease
references: Bardeesy N, et al. WT1 mutations in Denys-Drash syndrome. Nat Genet. 1994.
Miyagawa S, et al. Clinical features and management of Denys-Drash syndrome. Pediatr Nephrol. 2017.
Orphanet: Denys-Drash syndrome. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
